comment: What each CI job is expected to cost, in seconds. The Gate prints the run's real durations
beside these numbers and warns when one is over `tolerance` times its baseline (ADR 0020).
These are observed medians with a little headroom, not budgets and not promises: the xcode-27
preview image is variable, and the same job has been seen at 57 s and at 158 s with no change
to it at all. The point is that a change to the shape of the gate shows up on the run that
makes it, instead of being reconstructed by hand three pushes later — which is exactly what
happened when parallel UI testing took iPhone from 854 s to 936 s and broke iPad.
A job with no entry here is reported as unbaselined and warns, and a policy test refuses it: the
gate cannot wait for a job whose cost nobody wrote down. Its timeout is held to this number
too — at least twice it, and no more than four times it or five minutes, whichever is larger —
so a hung job stops in minutes instead of burning a runner for half an hour.
